`repotracer setup` first detects the environment and four host integrations—Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot—by checking each CLI and/or its expected config location; it also records whether the config already contains RepoTracer. The generic MCP option is always available but excluded from automatic host selection. [crates/cli/src/agents.rs:50-96](crates/cli/src/agents.rs:50) [crates/cli/src/setup.rs:10-35](crates/cli/src/setup.rs:10)

It normalizes the GPT scout configuration: Codex backends become `codex-cli` with a GPT model and a minimum timeout; OpenAI-compatible backends must use a `gpt-*` model; other backends fall back to Codex CLI with `gpt-5.6-luna`. Non-dry runs verify the Codex executable and login status. [crates/cli/src/setup.rs:106-165](crates/cli/src/setup.rs:106)

Selection uses all detected integrations during `--dry-run`, allowing the dry-run to show the complete plan; normal setup selects only detected hosts. Each selected host receives native MCP configuration plus routing assets: Claude gets a skill, Codex gets TOML MCP plus `AGENTS.md`, Cursor gets MCP plus a project rule, and Copilot gets MCP plus project instructions. [crates/cli/src/setup.rs:171-176](crates/cli/src/setup.rs:171) [crates/cli/src/agents.rs:175-238](crates/cli/src/agents.rs:175)

`repotracer uninstall` requires `--yes`; it removes RepoTracer MCP entries from all host configs, removes skills/rules, strips managed instruction blocks, and deletes the local RepoTracer config while preserving provider logins and the binary. [crates/cli/src/setup.rs:179-193](crates/cli/src/setup.rs:179) [crates/cli/src/agents.rs:362-416](crates/cli/src/agents.rs:362)

Read, Glob, and Grep are repository-scoped through `resolve_in_root`: relative inputs are joined to the configured root, lexical `..` escapes are rejected, and existing symlink targets are canonicalized and rechecked. Grep additionally runs `rg` with the repository as its working directory and passes only the validated relative path.

`RepoTools::call_many` delegates to `execute_tools`. It schedules calls in a `FuturesUnordered`, starts at most `concurrency` calls at once (default 8), and wraps every call in a per-call timeout (default 10 seconds). A timeout becomes a failed `ToolResult` with a deterministic error message.

Results complete concurrently but are stored by original index and collected in input order. Glob’s own result order is deterministic too: newest modification time first, then path as a tie-breaker.

Outputs are bounded: Read limits files to 10 MiB, reads to 2,000 lines and 2,000 characters per line, and final output to 32 KiB; Glob limits results to 100 paths/32 KiB; Grep limits output to 100 lines/32 KiB. Regression tests cover root and symlink escapes, concurrent execution/order, and truncation/continuation behavior for all three tools.

Read, Glob, and Grep are repository-scoped: each resolves its user-supplied path through `resolve_in_root`; Grep also runs `rg` with the repository as its working directory. Read rejects files over 10 MiB and caps output at 2,000 lines/2,000 characters per line/32 KiB; Glob and Grep cap results at 100 entries/lines and 32 KiB, returning continuation guidance when truncated. Glob additionally excludes common generated/dependency directories and sorts matches deterministically (newest first, then path).

`RepoTools::call_many` sends calls to `execute_tools`, which maintains at most the configured number in flight (default 8), starts additional calls only as slots free, and wraps every call in a per-tool timeout (default 10 seconds). Completed futures may arrive in any order, but each result is stored by its input index and collected in input order; timeouts become failed `ToolResult`s with a deterministic timeout reminder.

Regression tests cover concurrent execution and input-order preservation, plus bounded Glob and Grep output with continuation notices. The repository has no dedicated timeout test in the inspected tool-test module; timeout behavior is implemented directly in the executor.

`RepoTools` constructs Read, Glob, and Grep with one repository root and dispatches calls only to those tools. Each tool resolves its requested path/directory through `resolve_in_root`; Grep also runs `rg` with the repository as its working directory and explicitly prevents glob traversal outside it. Read rejects oversized files, while Glob caps returned matches with `DEFAULT_LIMIT`.

`call_many` delegates to `execute_tools`: it maintains a bounded in-flight set (`concurrency`, default 8), starts calls concurrently, wraps every call in `tokio::time::timeout`, and returns a synthetic failed result on expiry. Although completions arrive through `FuturesUnordered`, each result is stored by its original index and collected in input order, making output deterministic.

The regression test verifies genuine overlap (four 500-ms calls complete under 1.2 s with peak concurrency ≥2) and verifies returned IDs retain input order.
